text: [serious, cinematic storyteller, brisk pace] In thirty days, his followers took eleven cities. They didn't need weapons. They only needed crowds. In every city, the same thing happened. The people who knew how things worked were pushed aside… and the loudest voices took their place. A man with no training ran the hospital. A man who could barely read rewrote the schools. A new bridge was built by people who had never built anything. On the day it opened, the crowds cheered. On the third night, it fell. No one was on it. Not yet. The engineers who warned them had already been silenced. A man once asked the Prophet when the Hour would come. He said: when trust is lost. And when authority is handed to those unfit for it. Across the country, the experts packed their bags. The loud ones stayed. And in the capital, the man from nowhere gave his next order: close the libraries.
